name: Sanjay Chandra v. CBI
holding: Bail is the rule and jail the exception; pre-trial detention should not be punitive, even in economic offences, where the accused is not shown to be a flight risk or likely to tamper with evidence.

name: Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI
holding: Laid down guidelines categorising offences for bail and stressed that arrest should not be routine; urged a dedicated bail law.

name: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab
holding: Anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC should not be hedged by rigid conditions; grant is a matter of judicial discretion on the facts of each case.

name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
holding: Arrest is not automatic for offences punishable up to seven years; police must apply the Section 41 CrPC checklist and record reasons.

name: Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb
holding: Prolonged incarceration can justify bail even where a statute such as UAPA restricts it, because the constitutional right under Article 21 prevails.

name: Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy v. CBI
holding: Economic offences form a class apart and call for a different approach to bail, given their gravity and effect on the economy.

name: State of Gujarat v. Mohanlal Jitamalji Porwal
holding: Economic offences are committed with deliberate design for personal gain and affect the community's economy, so they must be viewed seriously.

name: State of U.P. v. Amarmani Tripathi
holding: Relevant bail factors include the nature and gravity of the accusation, severity of punishment, danger of tampering with witnesses and reasonable apprehension of the accused absconding.

name: NIA v. Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali
holding: Under Section 43D(5) UAPA, at the bail stage the court asks only whether the material shows the accusation is prima facie true, without weighing evidence in detail.
